10, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who spent 12 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{cite web|author=Kennedy|first=Alex|date=June 2, 2017|title=Kwame Brown opens up about his NBA career, facing criticism, Michael Jordan and more|url=https://hoopshype.com/2017/06/02/kwame-brown-opens-up-about-his-nba-career-facing-criticism-michael-jordan-and-more/|access-date=March 30, 2018|website=Hoops Hype}} Selected [[NBA first overall draft pick|first overall]] by the [[Washington Wizards]] in the [[2001 NBA draft]], Brown was the first player to be drafted number one overall straight out of high school.{{Cite web|url=https://www.allaboutbasketball.us/uncategorized/nba-high-school-draft-picks.html|title = List of NBA High School Draft Picks}}{{Cite web|url=https://listafterlist.com/nba-basketball-players-straight-from-high-school/|title=NBA Basketball Players Straight from High School – ListAfterList|date=December 29, 2017 }} He later played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Memphis Grizzlies]], [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Golden State Warriors]], and [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/gallery/biggest-draft-busts-kwame-brown-michael-olowokandi-sam-bowie-darko-milicic-062512|title=Biggest draft busts in NBA history|date=October 20, 2016|website=foxsports.com|access-date=May 24, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.thesportster.com/basketball/nba-draft-bust-disappointment-injuries/|title=The Biggest Bust In Each NBA Draft From The 2000s|date=May 4, 2020|website=TheSportster|access-date=May 24, 2020}} ==High school== Brown was consistently rated as the "best high school player" in his class, which also included high school standouts [[Eddy Curry]] and [[Tyson Chandler]]. He was the high school player of the year as a senior in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. Brown finished his high school career at the historic [[Glynn Academy]] (in [[Brunswick, Georgia]]) as the school's all-time leading rebounder (1,235) and shot-blocker (605), and also finished second all-time as a scorer (1,539 points). He was named to the [[2001 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2001 McDonald's All-American]] Team. Brown's senior averages were 20.1 points, 13.3 rebounds, 5.8 blocks, 3 assists and 2 steals per game. While Brown was a senior, Glynn Academy produced a 24–7 record and reached the GHSA semifinals.{{Cite web|url=http://www.ghsbp.com/state/brackets/2001aaaaab.html|title=State Tournaments: 2001 AAAA boys}} ==Professional career== ===Washington Wizards (2001–2005)=== Originally signing a letter of intent to play for the [[University of Florida]], he later declared for the [[2001 NBA draft]]. The [[Washington Wizards]], under team president [[Michael Jordan]], used their first overall pick on him. Following a pre-draft workout with the Wizards, it had been reported that Brown told then-Wizards coach [[Doug Collins (basketball)|Doug Collins]], "If you draft me, you'll never regret it."[https://www.usatoday.com/sports/nba/01draft/stories/2001-06-28-wiz.htm Wizards love top pick's skills] – Retrieved July 1, 2006 Perhaps as a result of hype and high expectations, Brown's rookie season was marred by a lack of maturity and production on the court.{{cite journal|last=Jenkins|first=Sally|title=Growing Pains|journal=Washington Post Magazine|date=April 21, 2002|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2006/11/28/AR2006112800709_pf.html|access-date=July 11, 2010}} In his rookie year, Brown averaged 4.5 points and 3.5 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/WAS/2002.html|title=2001-02 Washington Wizards Roster and Stats|work=Basketball Reference|access-date=22 December 2022}} However, the Wizards believed in Brown's potential.{{citation needed|date=June 2022}} In his second season as a professional, Brown saw more action in the league. He started 20 out of the 80 games he played and the total minutes he played doubled. Brown improved his numbers, posting averages of 7.4 points and 5.3 rebounds per game. In his third season, Brown continued to improve, posting career highs in both points (10.9) and rebounds (7.4). In a game against the [[Sacramento Kings]], he registered 30 points and 19 rebounds.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/240317027|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222050715/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/240317027|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 22, 2022|title=Brown gets career highs: 30 points, 19 boards|work=ESPN|location=Washington|agency=The Associated Press|date=18 March 2004|access-date=22 December 2022}} After his first three years in Washington, Brown rejected a five-year, $30 million contract offer, electing instead to test the free agent market when his contract expired after the season.{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2005/05/04/wizards-suspend-kwame-brown/7c970c43-9d7f-43f7-8ca5-285c50c3562d/|title=Wizards Suspend Kwame Brown|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=4 May 2005|access-date=22 December 2022|last=Lee|first=Michael}} In his fourth season, Brown was limited to 42 games due to injuries. His highest-scoring game of the season was 19 points,{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/250420018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221222050727/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/250420018|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 22, 2022|title=Hughes, Arenas sit out 4th quarter as Wizards prep for Bulls|work=ESPN|agency=The Associated Press|date=20 April 2005|access-date=22 December 2022|location=New York}} compared to his season-high of 30 the year before, and he averaged 7.0 points per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/WAS/2005.html|title=2004-05 Washington Wizards Roster and Stats|access-date=22 December 2022|work=Basketball Reference}} Late in the season, criticism increased; he feuded with [[Gilbert Arenas]], other teammates, and his coach [[Eddie Jordan (basketball)|Eddie Jordan]]. ===Los Angeles Lakers (2005–2008)=== On August 2, 2005, Brown and [[Laron Profit]] were traded to the Lakers in exchange for [[Caron Butler]] and [[Chucky Atkins]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2107572|title=Wizards to get Butler and Atkins|work=ESPN|date=14 July 2005|access-date=22 December 2022}} This move was met with some controversy from fans who disliked Brown's reputation and his label as an "under-achiever." In the beginning of the season, he averaged just above 6 points and 6 rebounds. On December 26, 2005, he played his first game at the Washington Wizards' MCI Center (now known as [[Capital One Arena]]) as a Laker. The sold-out crowd of 20,173 fans loudly booed him upon entering the game and whenever he touched the ball. In the second quarter, Brown was looking the other way when teammate [[Sasha Vujačić]] threw a pass his way. The ball bounced off his head and landed out of bounds, which was met with loud cheers from the crowd.{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2005/12/26/AR2005122601223_pf.html |title=Ex-Wizard Brown Calls Reception 'Weak' |last=Lee |first=Michael |date=December 27, 2005 |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |access-date=August 24, 2010 }} Brown called the reception "weak" and stated that "they should be cheering that I'm gone." The Wizards won the game 94–91. When Lakers center [[Chris Mihm]] went down with a season-ending ankle injury on March 12, 2006, Brown took over the starting center position. During his stint as a center, he raised his averages from 6.1 points and 6.3 rebounds to 12.3 points and 9.1 rebounds and started every game for the Lakers in the playoffs. Brown became a central part of the Lakers seven-game series with the [[Phoenix Suns]]. Although they ended up losing the series, it had appeared that Kwame Brown's potential was beginning to show. The surprising consistency Brown showed while playing center prompted Phil Jackson to make Brown the starting center in the 2006–07 season. Brown was injured at the beginning of the season and Mihm was also out with injury for the whole season, so the starting job at center was given to the young [[Andrew Bynum]]. After playing the majority of the minutes at center despite the bench role, he was given the starting job in early December. Brown again became injured in the 2007–08 season which allowed Bynum to start again at the center position where he flourished. However, when Bynum suffered a knee injury that appeared to jeopardize the Lakers' playoff chances, Brown regained his starting position. ===Memphis Grizzlies (2008)=== On February 1, 2008, Brown was traded along with [[Javaris Crittenton]], [[Aaron McKie]], the draft rights to [[Marc Gasol]], and the Lakers' [[2008 NBA Draft|2008]] and [[2010 NBA Draft|2010]] first-round draft picks for [[Pau Gasol]] and a second-round pick in 2010.{{cite news |last=Tillery |first=Ronald |title=Gasol traded to Lakers |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/news/2008/feb/01/gasol-traded-lakers/ |newspaper=[[Memphis Commercial Appeal]] |date=February 1, 2008 |access-date=February 1, 2008 }} On July 1, 2008, the Memphis Grizzlies chose not to sign Brown to a new contract, making him an unrestricted free agent. {{Citation needed|date=March 2008}} ===Detroit Pistons (2008–2010)=== On July 28, 2008, [[ESPN.com]] reported that the [[Detroit Pistons|Pistons]] signed Brown to a two-year deal worth $8 million, with the second year a player option.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3508699 |title=Dumars: Brown agrees to two-year deal with Pistons |last=Stein |first=Marc |date=July 29, 2008 |work=[[ESPN]] |access-date=August 24, 2010 }} ===Charlotte Bobcats (2010–2011)=== On August 23, 2010, Brown signed a one-year deal with the [[Charlotte Bobcats|Bobcats]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5489854 |title=Kwame Brown, Bobcats agree to deal |last=Stein |first=Marc |work=[[ESPN]] |date=August 24, 2010 |access-date=August 24, 2010 }} ===Golden State Warriors (2011–2012)=== On December 14, 2011, Brown signed a one-year, $7 million contract with the [[Golden State Warriors|Warriors]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors_sign_kwame_brown_121411.html | title=Warriors Sign Kwame Brown | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=December 14, 2011 | access-date=December 15, 2011}} === Philadelphia 76ers (2012–2013) === On March 13, 2012, Brown, along with [[Monta Ellis]] and [[Ekpe Udoh]], was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in exchange for [[Andrew Bogut]] and [[Stephen Jackson]]. Brown never played for the Bucks during the season.{{cite web|date=March 13, 2012|title=Bucks Acquire Monta Ellis, Ekpe Udoh and Kwame Brown from Warriors|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-monta-ellis-ekpe-udoh-and-kwame-brown-warriors|access-date=March 14, 2012|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc}}{{cite web|title=Ilyasova Free Agency Tour set to begin|date=July 5, 2012 |url=http://journaltimes.com/sports/basketball/bucks-beat-ilyasova-free-agency-tour-set-to-begin/article_4e562cd0-c709-11e1-9fed-0019bb2963f4.html}} On July 20, 2012, Brown signed a two-year contract for nearly $6 million with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-free-agent-center-kwame-brown | title=Sixers Sign Free Agent Center Kwame Brown| work=NBA.com | date=July 20, 2012 | access-date=July 20, 2012}} After sustaining a right hamstring strain in September 2013,{{cite web|url=http://fansided.com/2013/09/27/philadelphia-76ers-center-kwame-brown-suffers-strained-right-hamstring/|title=Philadelphia 76ers' center Kwame Brown suffers strained right hamstring|date=September 27, 2013|website=fansided.com|access-date=March 30, 2018}} Brown was waived by the 76ers on November 20 before appearing in a game for them in the [[2013–14 Philadelphia 76ers season|2013–14 season]].{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14809|title=Philadelphia 76ers waive Kwame Brown and Darius Morris, sign Elliot Williams and Lorenzo Brown :InsideHoops|website=insidehoops.com|access-date=March 30, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140115145309/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14809|archive-date=January 15, 2014|url-status=dead}} ==Post-NBA career== In 2017, Brown was the fifth overall pick in the inaugural draft of the [[BIG3]] basketball league. In BIG3 Brown played for the 3 Headed Monsters, who made it to the finals and ended up losing to Trilogy 51–46.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2706914-big3-basketball-league-2017-draft-results-and-full-team-rosters|title=BIG3 Basketball League 2017 Draft Results and Full Team In 2002, Brown's hometown girlfriend, Joselyn Vaughn, moved into his Virginia home.{{cite news |last1=Nichols |first1=Rachel |title=Great Leap Forward |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/2002/11/21/great-leap-forward/a02f2dd4-a8c9-48b8-b0f5-02f9fcb66270/ |access-date=18 May 2021 |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |date=November 21, 2002}} Together they had three daughters. In 2019, Brown sued for [[child custody|custody]] of the children.{{cite news |title=Kwame Brown Sued by Baby Mama for Child Support |url=https://theblast.com/c/kwame-brown-child-support |access-date=18 May 2021 |work=The Blast |date=June 10, 2019 |language=en}} ===Legal issues=== In August 2003, Brown was arrested and charged with [[driving while intoxicated]] near his hometown of Brunswick.{{cite news |title=Kwame Brown arrested for DUI |url=https://www.walb.com/story/1409800/kwame-brown-arrested-for-dui/ |access-date=18 May 2021 |publisher=WALB |date=August 20, 2003}} In October 2007, Brown was arrested in Georgia and charged with [[disorderly conduct]] and interference with a law enforcement officer after an incident in which the driver of a car in which he was a passenger was arrested for driving drunk with a suspended license.{{cite news |title=Reports: Lakers' Brown charged in Ga. incident |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3046722 |access-date=18 May 2021 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=October 2, 2007 |language=en}} Brown was arrested on March 31, 2019, by Georgia police and charged with felony possession of edible marijuana
